macros.name: xintDecToString
macros.doc: \xintDecToString uses fixed point notation for the output.

macros.name: xintDecToStringREZ
macros.doc: \xintDecToStringREZ uses fixed point (decimal) notation for the output.

macros.name: xintDenominator
macros.doc: This macro parses the input and outputs A'/B', with A' as would be returned by \xintNumerator{f} and B' as would be returned by \xintDenominator{f}.

macros.name: xintDivFloor
macros.doc: Computes both the floored division and the remainder \xintDivFloor.

macros.name: xintDivMod
macros.doc: \xintDivMod{q1}{q2} outputs {floor(q1/q2)}{q1 - q2*floor(q1/q2)}.

macros.name: xintEven
macros.doc: \xintEven{f} returns 1 if the integer obtained by truncation is even, and 0 otherwise.

macros.name: xintFloat
macros.doc: The macro \xintFloat [P]{f} has an optional argument P which replaces the current value of \xinttheDigits. The fraction f is then printed in scientific notation with a rounding to P digits.

macros.name: xintFloat
macros.doc: The macro \xintFloat [P]{f} has an optional argument P which replaces the current value of \xinttheDigits. The fraction f is then printed in scientific notation with a rounding to P digits.

macros.name: xintFloatAdd
macros.doc: \xintFloatAdd [P]{f}{g} first replaces f and g with their float approximations f' and g' to P significant places or to the precision from \xintDigits. It then produces the sum f'+g', correctly rounded to nearest with the same number of significant places.

macros.name: xintFloatAdd
macros.doc: \xintFloatAdd [P]{f}{g} first replaces f and g with their float approximations f' and g' to P significant places or to the precision from \xintDigits. It then produces the sum f'+g', correctly rounded to nearest with the same number of significant places.

macros.name: xintFloatBinomial
macros.doc: \xintFloatBinomial[P]{x}{y} computes binomial coefficients with either \xinttheDigits or P digits of precision.

macros.name: xintFloatBinomial
macros.doc: \xintFloatBinomial[P]{x}{y} computes binomial coefficients with either \xinttheDigits or P digits of precision.

macros.name: xintFloatBraced
macros.doc: The experimental macro \xintFloatBraced[P]{f} does like \xintFloat but its output consists of three TeX-braced groups { ⟨sign bit⟩ }{ ⟨scientific exponent⟩ }{ ⟨full width mantissa with decimal point⟩ } It is provided for users knowing how to pick one or the other of these constituents from usage of auxiliary macros.

macros.name: xintFloatBraced
macros.doc: The experimental macro \xintFloatBraced[P]{f} does like \xintFloat but its output consists of three TeX-braced groups { ⟨sign bit⟩ }{ ⟨scientific exponent⟩ }{ ⟨full width mantissa with decimal point⟩ } It is provided for users knowing how to pick one or the other of these constituents from usage of auxiliary macros.

macros.name: xintFloatDiv
macros.doc: \xintFloatDiv [P]{f}{g} first replaces f and g with their float approximations f' and g' to P (or \xinttheDigits) significant places. It then correctly rounds the fraction f'/g' to nearest P-float.

macros.name: xintFloatDiv
macros.doc: \xintFloatDiv [P]{f}{g} first replaces f and g with their float approximations f' and g' to P (or \xinttheDigits) significant places. It then correctly rounds the fraction f'/g' to nearest P-float.

macros.name: xintFloatFac
macros.doc: \xintFloatFac[P]{f} returns the factorial with either \xinttheDigits or P digits of precision.

macros.name: xintFloatFac
macros.doc: \xintFloatFac[P]{f} returns the factorial with either \xinttheDigits or P digits of precision.

macros.name: xintFloatMul
macros.doc: \xintFloatMul [P]{f}{g} first replaces f and g with their float approximations f' and g' to P (or \xinttheDigits) significant places. It then correctly rounds the product f'*g' to nearest P-float.

macros.name: xintFloatMul
macros.doc: \xintFloatMul [P]{f}{g} first replaces f and g with their float approximations f' and g' to P (or \xinttheDigits) significant places. It then correctly rounds the product f'*g' to nearest P-float.

macros.name: xintFloatPFactorial
macros.doc: \xintFloatPFactorial[P]{x}{y} computes the product (x+1)...y.

macros.name: xintFloatPFactorial
macros.doc: \xintFloatPFactorial[P]{x}{y} computes the product (x+1)...y.

macros.name: xintFloatPow
macros.doc: \xintFloatPow [P]{f}{x} uses either the optional argument P or in its absence the value of \xinttheDigits. It computes a floating approximation to f^x.

macros.name: xintFloatPow
macros.doc: \xintFloatPow [P]{f}{x} uses either the optional argument P or in its absence the value of \xinttheDigits. It computes a floating approximation to f^x.

macros.name: xintFloatSqrt
macros.doc: \xintFloatSqrt[P]{f} computes a floating point approximation of f, either using the optional n precision P or the value of \xinttheDigits.

macros.name: xintFloatSqrt
macros.doc: \xintFloatSqrt[P]{f} computes a floating point approximation of f, either using the optional n precision P or the value of \xinttheDigits.

macros.name: xintFloatToDecimal
macros.doc: \xintFloatToDecimal [P]{f} does float rounding on input like \xintFloat then outputs the number using decimal notation, i.e. with as many zeros as are needed (and no more) and no scientific exponent.

macros.name: xintFloatToDecimal
macros.doc: \xintFloatToDecimal [P]{f} does float rounding on input like \xintFloat then outputs the number using decimal notation, i.e. with as many zeros as are needed (and no more) and no scientific exponent.

macros.name: xintFloor
macros.doc: \xintFloor {f} returns the largest relative integer N with N ⩽ f.

macros.name: xintFracToDecimal
macros.doc: \xintFracToDecimal is a variant of \xintFracToSci which differs from it in so far as it outputs a numerator using decimal notation, i.e. with as many zeros as are needed (and no more) and no scientific exponent.

macros.name: xintGeq
macros.doc: \xintGeq{f}{g} outputs 1 if |f| ⩾ |g| and 0 if not.

macros.name: xintGtorEq
macros.doc: \xintGtorEq{f}{g} returns 1 if f⩾ g, 0 otherwise.

macros.name: xintiCeil
macros.doc: \xintiCeil {f} does the same as \xintCeil but its output is without the /1[0].

macros.name: xintifCmp
macros.doc: \xintifCmp{ ⟨f⟩ }{ ⟨g⟩ }{ ⟨if f<g⟩ }{ ⟨if f=g⟩ }{ ⟨if f>g⟩ } compares its first two arguments and chooses accordingly the correct branch.

macros.name: xintifInt
macros.doc: \xintifInt{f}{YES branch}{NO branch} expandably chooses the YES branch if f reveals itself after expansion and simplification to be an integer.

macros.name: xintiFloor
macros.doc: \xintiFloor {f} does the same as \xintFloor but without the trailing /1[0].

macros.name: xintifNotZero
macros.doc: \xintifNotZero{ ⟨N⟩ }{ ⟨IsNotZero⟩ }{ ⟨IsZero⟩ } expandably checks if the first mandatory argument f is not zero or is zero.

macros.name: xintifOdd
macros.doc: \xintifOdd{ ⟨N⟩ }{ ⟨odd⟩ }{ ⟨not odd⟩ } expandably checks if the first mandatory argument f, after truncation to an integer, is odd or even.

macros.name: xintifZero
macros.doc: \xintifZero{ ⟨f⟩ }{ ⟨IsZero⟩ }{ ⟨IsNotZero⟩ } expandably checks if the first mandatory argument N (a number, possibly a fraction if xintfrac is loaded, or a macro expanding to one such) is zero or not.

macros.name: xintiRound
macros.doc: \xintiRound{x}{f} returns the integer equal to 10^x times what \xintRound{x}{f} would return.

macros.name: xintiTrunc
macros.doc: \xintiTrunc{x}{f} returns the integer equal to 10^x times what \xintTrunc{x}{f} would produce.

macros.name: xintModTrunc
macros.doc: \xintModTrunc {q1}{q2} computes q1 - q2*t(q1/q2) with t(q1/q2) equal to the truncated division of two fractions q1 and q2.

macros.name: xintPFloat
macros.doc: \xintPFloat [P]{f} is like \xintFloat but ``pretty-prints'' the output.

macros.name: xintPFloat
macros.doc: \xintPFloat [P]{f} is like \xintFloat but ``pretty-prints'' the output.

macros.name: xintPFloatMinTrimmed
macros.doc: • \xintPFloatMinTrimmed is the minimal number of trailing zeros which have to be present to activate actual trimming.

macros.name: xintPow
macros.doc: \xintPow{f}{x}: computes f^x with f a fraction and the exponent x possibly also, but if only xintfrac is loaded it will be truncated to an integer.

macros.name: xintREZ
macros.doc: \xintREZ Removes trailing zeros from A and B and adjust the N in A/B[N].

macros.name: xintSub
macros.doc: Computes the difference of two fractions (\xintSub{F}{G} computes F-G).

macros.name: xintTFrac
macros.doc: \xintTFrac{f} returns the fractional part, f=trunc(f)+frac(f).

macros.name: xintTTrunc
macros.doc: \xintTTrunc{f} truncates to an integer (truncation towards zero).
